argument:
AppLovin's 53% revenue growth, 77.68% GAAP operating margin and 64% continuing-profit growth provide a strong realised operating case. Q2 FCF of $863.3m compares favorably with only $461.8m net debt, limiting near-term financing dependence. At 21.68x trailing and estimated 13.29x forward earnings, continued execution could deliver attractive earnings participation without requiring a higher multiple.

Receivables rose to $2.171bn and FCF was about 68% of continuing net income, so accounting profits are not identical to cash. Platform dependence and exceptional margins remain meaningful durability risks. Nevertheless, cash generation and modest net leverage provide a measurable cushion. The deeply negative price trend supplies no bottom confirmation; this is a conditional business-value purchase requiring economics to persist, rather than an oversold technical recommendation.
key_points: Strong growth and GAAP operating profitability support the earnings case.
Observed FCF is substantial relative to modest net debt.
Receivables, platform durability and unconfirmed price recovery constrain sizing and timing.
